## TL;DR

Review round 4 returned the post-merge summary feature with one finding: summary-state persistence failures are silent — lost status writes map to `idle`, the CLI polls only for terminal statuses, and GET errors are suppressed, so a committed report can still cost a 15-minute hang and a failed generation can vanish from view. I made lost writes loud (boolean result plus server log), taught polling to treat a committed `summary.md` as terminal, and made persistent fetch failures fail fast. New unit, helper, and end-to-end CLI tests cover each path, and the drawer already renders the report whenever the file exists regardless of status.

## Work and rationale

**Loud persistence.** `writeSummaryStatus` now returns a boolean and logs to the server log on failure instead of swallowing the error. All three call sites (pending, done, failed) inherit the logging; generation outcome semantics are unchanged — a lost `done` write still reports success because the committed file is ground truth. The `read → idle` mapping stays: it is now harmless because every consumer that matters (CLI polling, the drawer block) also keys off the report file's existence.

**Exists-aware polling.** `cmdSummary` previously returned only on `done`/`failed` and swallowed every GET error until the 15-minute timeout. The poll predicate moved into an exported `isSummaryPollTerminal` helper (`done`, `failed`, or `exists`), and the loop into `pollSummaryState`, which counts consecutive fetch failures and throws a 503 after ten instead of hanging. The CLI success message prints whenever the report exists, not just on `done`.

**Drawer resilience.** No drawer change was needed: the Report pane renders the markdown whenever the file exists, independent of the status value, so a lost status never hides a committed report. A lost `failed` status is now visible in the server log at minimum, and the normal path still records it.

## Approaches tried

I considered throwing from `writeSummaryStatus` instead of returning a boolean, but the queue path deliberately never throws (fire-and-forget must not disturb landing), so a return value plus logging fits all callers without restructuring. I considered synthesizing `done` in `readSummaryStatus` when the file exists but the status is unreadable, but that would conflate layers — the GET route already returns `exists` alongside `status`, and pushing synthesis into the reader would surprise its other callers. For the CLI fail-fast I first inlined the counter, then extracted `pollSummaryState` with injectable budgets so the striking behavior is unit-testable without a server.

## Challenges and blockers

The first full gate run after these edits failed typecheck: the new `it.each` table passes plain strings where the helper wants the status union. I exported `TaskSummaryState` from the CLI module and cast at the call site rather than weakening the helper. The review's visual-evidence note asks for the drawer Report view again; no preview fixture can seed a real `summary.md`, so the summary block cannot render on the preview board — a declared shot would either fail handoff (missing highlight) or prove nothing (bare drawer). Shots stay skipped with this justification, as in prior rounds. The engineering draft from the previous handoff was consumed into `round-3.json` as designed, so this is a fresh draft.

## Key learnings

- Advisory persistence must still be observable: returning a status instead of swallowing keeps fire-and-forget semantics while ending silent loss.
- Polling should key off the artifact, not the bookkeeping: the report file existing is a stronger terminal signal than any status write.
- Extracting CLI poll loops into injectable helpers turns timing-sensitive network behavior into fast deterministic unit tests plus a thin e2e shell.
